subject: Sprint-0 intake: VPC/on-prem environment & validation checkpoints
thread_body:
From: Amit Shah <amit@orbitalhealth.io>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Lopez <d.lopez@orbitalhealth.io>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint-0 intake: VPC/on-prem environment & validation checkpoints

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — team is excited to move toward a private deployment. We wanted to kick off a short sprint-zero intake to make sure we capture network, KMS, and account prerequisites so the engineering kickoff is frictionless. High-level asks from our side:

- Target architecture doc (VPC peering vs. private link recommendations)
- Expected IP ranges, firewall egress rules, and NAT/eBPF constraints
- Service account model and minimum permissions required
- KMS integration options (bring-your-own vs. Redwood-managed)
- Any certs/CA requirements for mutual TLS between on-prem gateway and Redwood runtime

Would you be able to send a concise checklist we can run against our ops team? Also happy to schedule a 30-min intake to walk the list.

Appreciate it —
Amit
Principal Cloud Architect
Orbital Health

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Amit Shah <amit@orbitalhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-0 intake: VPC/on-prem environment & validation checkpoints

Hi Amit — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a sprint-zero intake checklist and a blank service-account inventory you can populate. Below is a prioritized checklist (we keep it intentionally short for the ops runbook):

1) Network & connectivity
   - Confirm CIDR blocks for primary and peered VPCs (example: 10.10.0.0/16)
   - List required outbound ports (TCP 443, 80; UDP if using metrics agents)
   - Egress destinations to allow: registry.redwood.ai:443, s3 endpoints, metrics endpoints (we provide exact prefixes)
   - NAT/Gateway: ensure stable SNAT IPs for egress allowlisting
   - BGP/Peering: share ASN if using transit; if using PrivateLink, confirm region and service endpoints

2) Identity & service accounts
   - Create dedicated service account (least-privilege) for Redwood runtime with the following scopes: read-only S3, secrets access to specified KMS key, cloudwatch/logging write (or equivalent).
   - Populate and share service_account_inventory.csv (attached)

3) Cryptography & secrets
   - KMS approach: we support both BYOK and Redwood-managed. For BYOK, provide key ARN and policy allowing Redwood principal.
   - TLS: if using mutual TLS, provide CA bundle and expected CN patterns. We can also terminate TLS at our layer if necessary.

4) DNS & certs
   - If using private DNS, provide zone details and delegation plan.
   - Confirm if wildcard certs are available or if Redwood should provision certs via partner CA.

5) Compliance evidence & logging
   - Retention window requirement (days)
   - Log export destination (S3 bucket or on-prem syslog) and ARN/URL

6) Operational items
   - Outage contact list and Bay/Region SLA expectations
   - Preferred maintenance windows for rolling updates

Attach: sprint_zero_network_map.png (network diagram), service_account_inventory.csv (template), sow_draft_v1.pdf (draft SOW).

Next steps:
- Amit, can you confirm who will own the service_account_inventory?
- If you’re up for it, here’s a calendar link to grab a 30-min intake: https://calendar.redwood.ai/book/30min/tessa_morgan/slot

Thanks — copying Marissa and Ben for any additional technical notes.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick add: two items from the runtime team we often miss in sprint-zero that cause delays:

- KMS key policy must include an explicit condition for cross-account use if Orbital wants to keep key in their account; please include the AWS account ID and principal ARN to avoid policy churn.
- Service account token rotation: indicate if you have an automated rotation process (we support short-lived tokens via our connector, but need an agreed TTL).

If handy, include a contact for your security engineer so we can exchange a short threat model and mutual TLS cert fingerprints ahead of the intake call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
